plastic.recommended_action: Recycle in Plastic / Dry Waste Bins
disposal_instructions: Empty all contents completely.
Rinse with clean water to remove residue.
Remove non-recyclable caps/labels if required by local guidelines.
Crush or flatten container to save bin space.
reuse_ideas: Cut plastic bottles to create self-watering seed planters for small herbs.
Organize small items (desk stationery, screws, buttons) using cut plastic bases.
Create a bird feeder by inserting wooden spoons through a clean plastic bottle.
upcycling_ideas: Transform rigid plastic bottles into hanging vertical garden planters.
Weave plastic bags into durable water-resistant tote bags or outdoor mats.
Craft decorative desk lamps or pencil holders using colored plastic containers.
safety_warnings: Do NOT burn plastic items — burning releases toxic dioxins and carcinogens into the air.
Never re-use single-use plastic bottles (PET #1) for warm or acidic liquids over extended periods.

disposal_instructions: Empty contents and rinse clean.
Remove metal lids or plastic caps and recycle them separately.
Separate colored glass (green, amber) from clear glass if required locally.
Never mix light bulbs, mirrors, or ceramics with container glass.
reuse_ideas: Use clean glass jars as food storage containers, spice jars, or beverage glasses.
Store dry goods (rice, beans, pasta, nuts) in airtight glass jars.
Use as small flower vases, candle holders, or pencil stands.
upcycling_ideas: Craft customized painted glass lantern votives using fairy lights.
Build a decorative terrarium with pebbles, moss, and succulents inside a glass jar.
Cut glass bottles to make unique drinking glasses or candle holders.
safety_warnings: Wrap broken glass in thick newspaper or cardboard before disposal to protect sanitation workers.
Handle sharp edges with heavy-duty protective gloves.

metal.recommended_action: Recycle in Metal / Can Recycling Bins
disposal_instructions: Rinse food or beverage residue thoroughly.
Push sharp tin can lids inside the can or fold edges down safely.
Clean and ball up aluminum foil (balls larger than 2 inches can be recycled).
reuse_ideas: Use clean metal tins as desk organizers, cutlery holders, or paint brush cups.
Pinch metal pop tabs to create picture frame hanging hooks.
Use sturdy food cans as small potted plant holders.
upcycling_ideas: Punch decorative hole patterns into metal cans to create outdoor candle lanterns.
Construct wind chimes using various metal bottle caps and tin lids.
Transform larger metal drums or tins into rustic indoor planters.
safety_warnings: Beware of jagged tin edges when opening or washing metal cans.
Do not puncture pressurised aerosol cans or expose them to direct heat.

disposal_instructions: Keep paper dry and free from oil, grease, or food stains.
Remove plastic wrappings, metal spiral binders, and excessive tape.
Shred sensitive personal documents before recycling.
reuse_ideas: Use waste paper as protective wrapping material for fragile items when shipping.
Use blank backs of printed sheets for scratch pads or note taking.
Compost shredded untreated paper into garden soil.
upcycling_ideas: Craft handmade recycled paper sheets with embedded dried flower petals.
Create papier-mâché sculptures, bowls, or decorative masks.
Fold newspaper into biodegradable seed starter pots for gardening.
safety_warnings: Soiled paper (e.g. greasy pizza boxes, food wrappers) cannot be recycled and should be composted or disposed of as general waste.

disposal_instructions: Flatten all boxes completely to conserve recycling collection space.
Remove packing peanuts, bubble wrap, and heavy plastic shipping tape.
Ensure cardboard is dry and free of heavy oil/grease.
reuse_ideas: Reuse shipping boxes for home storage, moving, or mailing packages.
Lay flattened cardboard on garden beds as a natural weed barrier/mulch layer.
Use cardboard sheets as surface protection during DIY painting or craft projects.
upcycling_ideas: Build creative cardboard playhouses, scratch posts for cats, or toy furniture.
Construct sturdy drawer organizers or desktop document dividers.
Craft decorative wall art tiles using woven corrugated cardboard strips.
safety_warnings: Wet or moldy cardboard must not go into paper recycling streams.

organic.recommended_action: Compost in Organic Waste Bin / Garden Compost
disposal_instructions: Separate food waste and organic peels from all plastic packaging.
Place in dedicated green organic waste bin or home compost pit.
Keep meat/dairy out of open home compost pits to avoid attracting pests.
reuse_ideas: Use vegetable scraps (onion skins, carrot ends, celery tops) to simmer homemade broth.
Use citrus peels to make natural vinegar household cleaning spray.
Crush dried eggshells into plant soil for a slow-release calcium boost.
upcycling_ideas: Start a vermicomposting worm bin to produce rich organic fertilizer.
Use avocado pits or fruit seeds to germinate household houseplants.
Extract natural plant dyes from onion skins or avocado stones for fabrics.
safety_warnings: Avoid leaving organic food waste uncovered indoors to prevent fruit flies and bacteria proliferation.

e_waste.recommended_action: Take to Certified E-Waste Recycling Drop-Off Center
disposal_instructions: NEVER throw electronic devices into general household trash.
Perform a factory reset and erase personal data before disposal.
Remove rechargeable batteries if removable and recycle separately.
reuse_ideas: Repurpose an old smartphone as a dedicated home security camera or digital desk clock.
Donate working functional electronics to local schools, charities, or refurbishment non-profits.
Use old tablet screens as dedicated digital photo frames.
upcycling_ideas: Repurpose circuit boards into retro jewelry, keychains, or coaster art.
Turn obsolete computer hard drive platters into decorative mirrors or wind chimes.
safety_warnings: Do NOT dismantle electronic screens or CRT monitors — they contain hazardous heavy metals like lead and mercury.

hazardous.recommended_action: Deliver to Household Hazardous Waste Collection Center
disposal_instructions: Store batteries, chemicals, and medical waste in sealed original containers.
Keep hazardous materials segregated from all household recyclables.
Drop off at designated municipal hazardous waste collection points.
reuse_ideas: Rechargeable batteries should be recharged and reused hundreds of times rather than discarded.
upcycling_ideas: No upcycling recommended for hazardous items due to chemical safety risks.
safety_warnings: CRITICAL: Damaged lithium-ion batteries can catch fire or explode if crushed in trash trucks.
Never incinerate or throw batteries into household fires.

general_waste.recommended_action: Dispose in General Landfill Waste Bin
disposal_instructions: Bag residual non-recyclable waste securely before throwing into garbage bin.
Minimize non-recyclable item consumption by opting for reusable alternatives.
reuse_ideas: Inspect item to see if any components (like metal fasteners or plastic handles) can be salvaged before discarding.
upcycling_ideas: Use multi-layer composite waste materials for craft packing insulation if safe.
safety_warnings: Ensure non-recyclable items do not contaminate clean recycling streams.
